body.statement: For every compatible \(p\), dose \(d\), and endpoint in \(\{\underline\theta_d(p),\overline\theta_d(p)\}\), there exists \(q^\star\in\Gamma_L(p)\) attaining that endpoint with \(|\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)|\le3L-2\). For rational \(p\), one can construct \(q^\star\) with rational masses from the active facet certificate and complementary slackness.
body.justification: Sharpness requires compatible response-triple laws, not only valid dual inequalities.
body.gap: Two-way constructive tables are available in LuDingDasgupta2018; the present construction must honor a forbidden three-way support at every endpoint branch.
body.consumer: Endpoint-attaining mixtures provide transparent worst-case response profiles for benefit-risk reporting and sensitivity analysis.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a compatible marginal vector \(p\), a dose \(d\in\mathcal D\), and one of the two endpoint objectives.  We first use a finite-support linear-algebra argument to obtain attainment with the asserted support size.  Index the columns by \(u\in\mathcal U_L\), and let \(M\) be the \((3L-2)\)-by-\(|\mathcal U_L|\) matrix whose rows are indexed by \(\varnothing\) and by \((r,j)\in\mathcal D\times\{1,\ldots,L-1\}\), with
\[
 M_{\varnothing,u}=1,
 \qquad
 M_{(r,j),u}=\mathbf 1\{u_r=j\}.
\]
Define
\[
 b(p)=\bigl(1,(p_{rj})_{r\in\mathcal D,\,1\le j<L}\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Then
\[
 \Gamma_L(p)=\{q\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal U_L}:Mq=b(p)\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, every member of \(\Gamma_L(p)\) satisfies the equations in (1) by the definition of the coupling fiber.  Conversely, if \(q\ge0\) and \(Mq=b(p)\), the first row gives \(\sum_uq(u)=1\), and, for each \(r\in\mathcal D\), the omitted level-zero equation follows from
\[
 \sum_{u:u_r=0}q(u)
 =1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\sum_{u:u_r=j}q(u)
 =1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}p_{rj}
 =p_{r0},
\]
where the last equality uses that \((p_{rj})_{j\in\mathcal Y_L}\) is an arm probability vector.  This proves (1).

Compatibility of \(p\) means that (1) is nonempty.  It is closed and is contained in the finite-dimensional probability simplex, hence it is compact.  The map
\[
 q\longmapsto \theta_d(q)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}B_d(u)q(u)
\]
is linear and continuous, so it attains both its minimum and its maximum on \(\Gamma_L(p)\).

For either objective choose, among all optimizers, an optimizer \(q^\star\) having the smallest support, and write \(S=\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)\).  We claim that the columns \((M_u)_{u\in S}\) are linearly independent.  If not, there is a nonzero vector \(z\), supported on \(S\), such that \(Mz=0\).  Because every coordinate of \(q^\star\) on \(S\) is strictly positive, for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), both \(q^\star+\varepsilon z\) and \(q^\star-\varepsilon z\) are nonnegative and, by \(Mz=0\), satisfy (1).  If the objective is minimized, both perturbed objective values are at least the value at \(q^\star\); if it is maximized, both are at most that value.  Their average is exactly the value at \(q^\star\), so in either case both perturbed points are also optimal and
\[
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}B_d(u)z(u)=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
The first row of \(Mz=0\) gives \(\sum_uz(u)=0\).  Thus a nonzero \(z\) has both signs.  Setting
\[
 t=\min_{u\in S:z(u)<0}\frac{q^\star(u)}{-z(u)}>0
\]
makes \(q^\star+tz\) feasible and nonnegative, makes at least one formerly positive coordinate zero, and, by (2), preserves the endpoint objective.  This contradicts the minimality of \(|S|\).  Therefore the columns on \(S\) are independent, and consequently
\[
 |\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)|=|S|
 \le \operatorname{rank}(M)
 \le 3L-2.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next give the certificate-driven construction, using the nonnegative-slack form of complementary slackness.  Write a canonical facet row \(h_i\in\mathcal H_L\) as
\[
 a_i(p)+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}\theta\ge0,
 \qquad
 a_i(p)=\kappa_i+
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\alpha_{irj}p_{rj}.
\]
For every \(q\in\Gamma_L(p)\), marginalization in (1), the definition of \(\theta(q)\), and the definition of vertex slack give the exact identity
\[
 a_i(p)+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}\theta(q)
 =\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q(u)\ge0.
 \tag{4}
\]
The inequality follows because a canonical supporting row has \(s_{h_i}(u)\ge0\) for every legal response type.

For the lower endpoint, the sharp three-facet endpoint theorem supplies an attaining certificate \(\lambda\in\mathcal D_d^-\) such that
\[
 \sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i=e_d,
 \qquad
 \underline\theta_d(p)=-\sum_i\lambda_i a_i(p),
 \qquad
 \lambda_i\ge0.
 \tag{5}
\]
Apply (4) to a lower-endpoint optimizer.  Equations (4)--(5) imply
\[
 0=\underline\theta_d(p)+\sum_i\lambda_i a_i(p)
 =\sum_i\lambda_i
   \sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q^\star(u).
 \tag{6}
\]
Every summand in (6) is nonnegative.  Hence, if \(\lambda_i>0\) and \(q^\star(u)>0\), then \(s_{h_i}(u)=0\).

For the upper endpoint, the same theorem supplies an attaining certificate \(\mu\in\mathcal D_d^+\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_i\mu_i\beta_i=-e_d,
 \qquad
 \overline\theta_d(p)=\sum_i\mu_i a_i(p),
 \qquad
 \mu_i\ge0.
 \tag{7}
\]
Equations (4) and (7) similarly give
\[
 0=\sum_i\mu_i a_i(p)-\overline\theta_d(p)
 =\sum_i\mu_i
   \sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q^\star(u),
 \tag{8}
\]
so \(\mu_i>0\) and \(q^\star(u)>0\) imply \(s_{h_i}(u)=0\).

Thus the construction is finite and explicit.  Given an active endpoint certificate \(\rho\), where \(\rho=\lambda\) for the lower endpoint and \(\rho=\mu\) for the upper endpoint, form the common tight set
\[
 T_\rho=
 \{u\in\mathcal U_L:s_{h_i}(u)=0
       \text{ for every }i\text{ with }\rho_i>0\}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Equations (6) and (8) show that the restricted system
\[
 M_{T_\rho}q_{T_\rho}=b(p),
 \qquad q_{T_\rho}\ge0
 \tag{10}
\]
is nonempty.  Conversely, extend any solution of (10) by zero outside \(T_\rho\).  Identity (4), summed with weights \(\rho_i\), gives equality in (5) or (7), respectively; hence every such extension belongs to \(\Gamma_L(p)\) and attains the specified endpoint.  Starting from any solution of (10), the support-elimination argument leading to (3) produces one supported on at most \(3L-2\) response types.  Equivalently, one may enumerate subsets \(S\subseteq T_\rho\) of size at most \(3L-2\), retain those for which the columns of \(M_S\) are independent, solve \(M_Sq_S=b(p)\), and accept the first nonnegative solution.  Nonemptiness and (3) guarantee success.  This exposes the variables, equations, nonnegativity constraints, and finite search required by the construction.

Finally suppose that \(p\) is rational.  Each canonical facet row is integral.  On any fixed linearly independent certificate support, the equation \(\sum_i\rho_i\beta_i=\pm e_d\) has at most one solution, and that solution is rational because it is obtained from an integer full-column-rank system.  Thus the active support in (9) and all its zero-slack tests are available in exact arithmetic.  Choose a solution of (10) with linearly independent support \(S\), as above.  There is a set \(R\) of \(|S|\) rows for which the square integer matrix \(M_{R,S}\) is nonsingular.  The positive masses are uniquely determined by
\[
 q_S=M_{R,S}^{-1}b_R(p).
\]
Because \(b_R(p)\) is rational, Cramer's rule shows that every coordinate of \(q_S\) is rational.  Checking the remaining equations of (10) and nonnegativity is again exact.  The resulting rational mixture is therefore a certificate-guided, complementary-slackness construction of an endpoint-attaining \(q^\star\in\Gamma_L(p)\), completing the proof.
